non_mechanical_rationales.reason: Common terminology and sentence precision are partly judgment-based; tests cover activation and fixtures, while review applies the prose judgment.
Inline versus display formatting depends on readability and importance; tests cover policy activation and reviewers decide borderline cases.
Common graph-theoretic and TCS terminology is discipline-specific and sometimes context-sensitive; review applies the policy after mechanical activation checks.
The amount of informal lead-in before a result depends on the result's role and local context.
Section outlines are prose-level checks; deterministic tests verify the requirement is active, and review assesses the paragraph quality.
Whether a proof is long or important enough for an opening paragraph is a mathematical writing judgment.
Equation display decisions depend on length, alignment, and importance; mechanical checks can only flag candidates for review.
Command-style sentence openings can be partly scanned mechanically, but deciding whether a standard disciplinary opening is clearer requires prose review.
